title: eval-harness: add CI prompt-regression & quality gating hooks for model rollouts
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: As we onboard new model variants and change prompt templates, we need automated regression checks and quality gates in CI so that model rollouts cannot regress prompt sets or reduce metric-level quality without explicit review. This PR adds lightweight CI hooks and an eval-harness integration that: 1) runs the baseline prompt-set regression tests as a gated job, 2) computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy/rouge/semantic-similarity depending on eval type), 3) fails the gate when regressions exceed configurable thresholds, and 4) emits artifacts with detailed diffs for triage. Changes are intentionally incremental: a new 'eval-gate' CI job, a small harness runner wrapper, and quality threshold config driven from .harness/config/*. Checklist: - [x] add CI job definition for GitHub Actions - [x] implement eval-harness runner wrapper (ci/eval_gate.py) - [x] add default threshold config and README - [x] wire artifacts/upload for triage - [x] tests for regression detection (unit + integration smoke) Notes: The description below includes the high-level commit summary and the files changed. See discussion for reviewer comments and decisions.

discussion: Luis Ortega: Overall this looks good. A few questions: how do we avoid flapping on noisy prompts? Can thresholds be overridden per-team?

Asha Menon: Yes, thresholds are hierarchical: repo-level defaults in .harness/config, overridable by .harness/config/<team>.yml and via linear deployment metadata (see docs). Also the gate supports a 'warning-only' mode for canaries.
Maya Patel: Test run flagged a small flake in the semantic similarity metric; recommend adding 5-run averaging before compare.
Asha Menon: Added 5-run smoothing in the runner and increased default sampling; updated tests to cover smoothing logic.
Ravi Singh: Approving after the lint fixes. CI failure in first run looked unrelated (transient infra), re-run passed.
Merge was approved via squash-and-merge after reviewers sign-off.
